transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um... I guess I'm here because of my eating. It's just... after my late shifts, I’ll stop for food, but then I kind of just keep going once I get home. Like, I'll finish a full takeout meal, and then move on to chips, or sweets... really just whatever is in the apartment. And... I don't know, afterward I'm just sort of shocked by how much I actually ate.
Do you feel guilty after these eating episodes?
Um... I guess. I mean... I don't really know if I'd call it guilt. I just... I don't feel great about it. I usually just try not to think about it too much after it happens.
Do you feel like you can stop eating once you've started on these late-night episodes?

Um... not really. It's... I guess it's hard to explain. Once I start on those nights... I don't know, it's almost like I'm watching myself from the outside. I'll be in my head telling myself to just put the food away, but... my hands just keep opening containers. I just keep going until everything is gone.
How often do these late-night eating episodes happen?

Um... probably at least once a week. Most weeks, anyway... ever since the apartment move settled into a normal routine. 

It just happens, and then... I don't know, when I eat way past what I meant to, I kind of feel like I have to make up for it. So I'll... I might just skip breakfast the next day, or force myself to go on a really long run. Or... sometimes I'll throw up. Just to... try and fix it, I guess.
How often do you throw up after one of these eating episodes?

Um... well, like I was just saying, since the apartment move settled into a routine, it's most weeks that I have at least one of those late nights... where I eat way past what I meant to. And... throwing up is just one of the ways I try to make up for it. 

I don't do it every single time. Sometimes I just skip breakfast or... force myself on that long run instead. So... I don't know exactly how often for that specifically. It just depends.
Do you usually feel hungry when these late-night eating episodes start?
Um... not always. Sometimes I am, I guess. But... mostly I don't really pay attention to that. I just... eat.
Do you usually feel stressed, anxious, or upset before these late-night eating episodes happen?
Um... I don't really know. I don't... pay much attention to how I'm feeling right before. Like I said, it just kind of happens.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

Um... yeah. I guess I am. I just... I get really panicky if my pants feel even a little tighter, or if the scale goes up just a pound. Even when people at the venue tell me I look too lean, I just... I worry that the guests or my coworkers will notice right away and think I let myself go.
Do you think you would still eat this way if you didn't worry about gaining weight?
I don't know. I haven't really... thought about it like that. I guess it's hard to imagine not worrying about it.
Do you think your late-night eating episodes would happen less often if you weren't worried about gaining weight?
I really couldn't say. Um... like I just said, I haven't really thought about it. Maybe? I just... I don't know if it would change anything.
Do you feel like you're in control of what you're eating during those late-night episodes?

No, not really. It's... um. Once I start eating on those nights, it's like I'm not even the one doing it. I'm just sort of... watching myself from the outside. I keep telling myself to stop, to just put the food away, but... my hands just keep opening containers. I just keep going until it's all gone.
Do you think your desire to eat late at night would go away if you weren't worried about your weight?
I... look, like I said a minute ago, I really don't know. You keep asking about the weight thing, but I just... I don't have an answer for that. I can't really picture it.
Do you usually throw up after these episodes because you feel uncomfortable or because you're trying to undo the calories you consumed?

Um... I guess it's the calories. Like, if I get home from work and eat too much takeout or snacks, I just... I go to the bathroom and make myself throw up. I just don't want it to sit in me and... turn into weight.
Is throwing up after eating mostly about undoing the calories you consumed or is it about feeling uncomfortable after eating?
I... didn't I just answer that? Like I said, it's... it's the calories. I just... yeah. That's pretty much it.
Is your main goal when throwing up after eating to get rid of the calories you just consumed?
Yeah... I mean, I thought I just said that. If I eat a bunch of takeout or whatever after work, I just... I make myself throw up so I don't gain weight from it. That's the main reason.
Is getting rid of the calories the only reason you throw up after eating, or are there other reasons as well?

I... I really don't know what else you want me to say. Like I've been saying, it's just about the weight. I get home, I eat too much of whatever, and I go to the bathroom to make myself throw up so it doesn't sit there. There's no... other reason. That's just what I do.
How many times a month do you throw up after eating?

I don't know the exact number... I guess since the apartment move settled into a routine, most weeks I have at least one late-night episode. I just eat way past what I meant to, and then... I try to make up for it. Sometimes by throwing up, or skipping breakfast the next day, or forcing a long run. So, maybe a few times a month for the throwing up part.
How often do you have episodes where you eat a large amount of food in a short time without trying to make up for it afterwards?
I... I don't really do that. If I eat like that, I always do something about it. I don't just leave it.
Do you typically throw up after eating, or do you use other methods like fasting or excessive exercise more often to compensate for the calories consumed?

I... I guess it's usually the other stuff. After a bad night of eating, I'll just... make myself run extra miles on the trail the next morning. Or I'll skip breakfast before my shift. Even when I'm really tired, I just... it feels like I have to undo it somehow.
Is your main goal when throwing up or using other methods like excessive exercise after eating to punish yourself or to prevent weight gain?

I guess... it's to prevent gaining weight. I don't really do it to punish myself. It's just... if my work pants feel even a little tighter, or the scale goes up a pound, I get kind of panicky. 

People at the venue actually tell me I look too lean sometimes, but... I just worry the guests and my coworkers will notice right away. I don't want them to think I let myself go.
